public_rationale: Contemporaneous reporting supports roughly ten million consumer subscribers. The retrieved cost evidence concerns company-wide compute expenses and includes annual projections. It does not establish that serving free ChatGPT users alone cost billions at the time. The subscriber component is supported, but the combined claim remains unresolved; there is no comparable free-tier cost evidence supporting a mixed or contradicted result.
limitations: Consumer subscriptions and business seats are different populations.
The annual cost interpretation is added because no cost period was stated.
Company-wide costs and later subscriber growth cannot settle this historical free-tier claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: ChatGPT's free version burns billions as a marketing channel for a product only ten million pay for.

statement.excerpt: ChatGPT’s free version is a poison in its system, a marketing channel that burns billions of dollars to introduce people to a product that only ten million people will actually pay for, and its future depends largely on its ability to continue convincing people to use it.

from_speaker: only ten million people will actually pay for
our_interpretation: The surrounding sentence expressly describes ten million existing paying subscribers. I therefore assess a contemporaneous observation, not a permanent ceiling on future subscriptions.
For the ongoing state, I use July through September 2024, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication. Contemporaneous subscriber observations within that quarter are relevant.
I read billions as an annual spending scale, rather than billions spent each quarter; the source does not state the cost period.
The cost measure must isolate serving free ChatGPT users. Total company losses, training expenses, and inference for paying customers or API users are not substitutes.
Ten million is an approximate consumer-subscription count. Business seats require separate treatment.
Poison is evaluative language and is not separately scored.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous records establish roughly ten million paying consumer subscribers and free-tier operating costs at a multibillion-dollar annual rate during the target period, with evidence that the tier serves user acquisition.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish materially different consumer subscriber numbers or free-tier costs below the claimed annual scale. Different-period or company-wide figures cannot supply that contradiction.
